chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Hard times on the road and lodging
summary: Small towns offer poor lodging; he always knew a woman in each town.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Was George Washington a funny person off the bandstand also?
He was one of the people that kept the band really happy while you were out on the road having bad times? I know you must have had some bad times out on the road.
Oh, you always, when you're traveling.
What were some of the worst things that happened out there?

Some of the places you go you can't get no place to stay, in these smaller towns, you know. Someone will say, "Well, you go to Miss Jones and she'll rent you a room," or something like that. It's better than nothing, so you just have to put up with it and go along with it.
Did you have to find the rooms or did the bandleader?
I didn't have to find nothing because when I was in school I had so many chicks I knew a chick in every town we played in - still have! When we got there, she had my room.
